## 1 Preparations

### 1.1 Obtain API information

To call API operations by using an SDK, you must obtain information that includes the service code, API operation name, and API version.

**Background information**

The information on the API directory page of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console is for reference only. For more information about how to call API operations, see the developer guides of cloud services. If the information on the API directory page is different from that in the developer guide of a cloud service, the information in the developer guide prevails.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Application Services** > **OpenAPI**
**Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Debugging**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, select the cloud service.
5. Select an API version from the **Version** drop-down list.
6. In the API list, you can view all API operations of the current version.

### 1.2 Obtain AccessKey credentials

AccessKey credentials are assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) or Security Token Service (STS). You can use one of the preceding types of AccessKey credentials for authentication when you call API operations.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of a request sender based on symmetric encryption. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt the signature string. AccessKey credentials can be assigned by RAM or STS: An AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. An AccessKey 3-tuple that is assigned by STS to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token.

**Obtain an AccessKey pair**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides two types of AccessKey pairs: those for personal accounts and those for organization accounts. We recommend that you use AccessKey pairs for personal accounts to call the API operations of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services. rations

> **Note:** Only operations administrators and level-1 organization administrators can obtain AccessKey pairs for organization accounts.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To use AccessKey pairs for personal accounts, you must configure the header parameters that are described in the following table for access control. Otherwise, an error that indicates insufficient permissions may occur.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region to which the instance that you want to access belongs. Example: cn- qingdao-****-****. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization to which the instance that you want to access belongs. For information about how to obtain the ID, see the "Obtain an organization ID" section of the Obtain the values of common request headers topic. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set to which the instance that you want to access belongs. For information about how to obtain the ID, see the "Obtain a resource set ID" section of the Obtain the values of common request headers topic. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance that you want to access. For example, you can view the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance in the ECS instance list. |

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and then click **User**
**Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of the personal account.

> **Note:** The AccessKey pair provides full access to cloud resources within your Alibaba Cloud account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

rations

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

> **Warning:** The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This ensures security.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you
want to obtain.
5. On the right side of the page that appears, click **Management AccessKey**.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

**Obtain an STS AccessKey 3-tuple**

STS allows you to use temporary credentials to access Apsara Stack resources. To call API operations in Apsara Stack by using STS, you must obtain an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token assigned by STS.
1. Obtain the RAM role.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. Click the profile picture in the upper-right corner of the page and then click User Information. iii. Click View Current Role Policy. iv. In the View Policies of Current Role dialog box, view your RAM role.
2. Obtain the endpoint of STS.
i. Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management console. ii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Project & Cluster O&M**. iii. In the **Products | Cluster** search box, enter **ascm-A**. iv. Find the cluster and click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column. v. On the cluster details page, click the **Desired State Configuration** tab. vi. In the list of files displayed on the left, click **kv.conf**. Then, click **Show Content** on the right. Press Ctrl+F and search for `region` and `internet-domain` to obtain their values.

```xml
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Create and initialize a DefaultAcsClient instance.
    // Specify your actual region ID, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey secret.
    DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("<yourRegionID>", "
<yourAccessKeyID>", "<yourAccessKeySecret>");
    HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
    clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
    clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTPS);
    profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);
    IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
    String assumeRole = callAssumeRole(client);
    if (StringUtils.isEmpty(assumeRole)) return;
    JSONObject assumeRoleJson = JSONObject.parseObject(assumeRole);
    JSONObject credentials = assumeRoleJson.getJSONObject("Credentials");
    // Obtain the STS AccessKey 3-tuple.
    String stsAK = credentials.getString("AccessKeyId");
    String stsSK = credentials.getString("AccessKeySecret");
    String stsToken = credentials.getString("SecurityToken");
```

```java
private static String callAssumeRole(IAcsClient client) {
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    // Replace "sts.aliyuns.com" with the endpoint of STS. The format of an endpoint
is sts-vpc.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}.
    request.setSysDomain("<sts.aliyuns.com>");
    request.setSysProduct("Sts");
    request.setSysAction("AssumeRole");
    request.setSysVersion("2015-04-01");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // The name of the role session. You can specify this parameter based on your bus
iness requirements. This parameter is usually set to the identity of the user who cal ls the API operation, such as the username. Replace "<yourRoleSessionName>" with your custom value.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleSessionName", "<yourRoleSessionName>");
    // The ARN of the RAM role. This role is a RAM role whose trusted entity is an AS
CM user. Replace "<yourRoleArn>" with the actual RAM role obtained in the first step.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleArn", "<yourRoleArn>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        return response.getData();
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
```

### 1.3 Obtain the values of common request headers

**request headers**

When you call Apsara Stack API operations, you must specify multiple common request headers. Then, common response parameters are returned in the results.

**Common request parameters**

You must specify the values of the common request parameters in the code to call Apsara Stack API operations.

| For example, you must replace | <yourResourceGroupID> | with the actual resourc |
|---|---|---|
| request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "<yourResourceGroupID>") |   |   |

use the SDK for Java to call API operations.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The region ID of the instance resource on which you want to perform operations. For more information, see Obtain a region ID. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization to which the instance resource belongs. For more information, see Obtain an organization ID. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set to which the instance resource belongs. For more information, see Obtain a resource set ID. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance to which the resource belongs. For more information, see Obtain an instance ID. |

| Note When you call API operations of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you do not need to use the x-acs-organizationid , x-acs-resourcegroupid , and x- acs-instanceid parameters. When you call API operations of other cloud services in Apsara Stack, you must use <x-acs-organizationid> to add the organization ID to the request header. Otherwise, the call fails and an error message indicating that you do not have permissions to initiate calls is returned. When you call API operations of other cloud services in Apsara Stack, we recommend that you use <x-acs-resourcegroupid> to add the resource set ID to the request header. After you specify the organization ID and the resource set ID, you can narrow down the query scope when you query instance resources. If you do not use <x-acs-resourcegroupid> to specify the resource set ID, the default resource set of the organization to which the user belongs is obtained. |   |   |

**Obtain a region ID**

You can view the region IDs of resources in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources** > **Regions**.
4. Click the name of the organization that you want to view.
5. In the **Regions** list, obtain the region ID from the **Region Name** column.

**Obtain an organization ID**

You must call a specific API operation to obtain the organization ID. You can obtain the organization ID by using the online debugging feature in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Application Services** > **OpenAPI**
**Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Debugging**.
4. Click the
icon, choose **Platform** > **Apsara Uni-manager**, and then select the **2019-**
**05-10** version.
5. Enter `GetOrganizationList` in the field to debug the operation online. Obtain the
organization ID from the **id** parameter in the **returned results**. For more information, see GetOrganizationList.

**Obtain a resource set ID**

You must call a specific API operation to obtain the resource set ID. You can obtain the resource set ID by using the online debugging feature in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Application Services** > **OpenAPI**
**Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Debugging**.
4. Click the
icon, choose **Platform** > **Apsara Uni-manager**, and then select the **2019-**
**05-10** version.
5. Enter `ListResourceGroup` in the field to debug the operation online. Obtain the resource
set ID from the **id** parameter in the **returned results**. For interface information, see ListResourceGroup.

**Obtain an instance ID**

You can obtain the ID of an instance in the cloud service console of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For example, you can view instance IDs in the ECS console.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Elastic Computing** > **Elastic Compute**
**Service**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Instances & Images** > **Instances**.
4. In the instance list that appears, view the instance IDs in the **Instance ID/Name** column.
rations

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| ResourceGroupName | The name of a resource set. |
| ResourceGroup | The ID of a resource set. |
| DepartmentName | The name of an organization. |
| Department | The ID of an organization. |

## 2 Use POP to make API calls

### 2.1 Obtain the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

**Apsara Uni-manager Management**

**Console**

To obtain the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can obtain the values of required variables in the Apsara Infrastructure Management console based on the configuration format of the endpoint and then concatenate the values. You can also search for the endpoint in the Apsara Infrastructure Management console.

**Background information**

To use the Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP) gateway to call API operations in Apsara Stack, you must obtain required service endpoints. You can obtain service endpoints from Apsara Stack onsite O&M engineers or by using one of the following methods.

**Method 1: Concatenate variable values to generate an**

**endpoint**

You can obtain the values of required variables and concatenate the values based on the configuration format of the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Configuration format of the endpoint in the central region: ascm.${global:internet-

```
domain}
```

Configuration format of the endpoint in the general region:

```
 ascm.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}
```

> **Note:** ${global:internet-domain} and ${global:region} are variables and need to be replaced with the actual values that you obtained. ${global:} is not included in the final endpoint.

**Obtain actual values of variables**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform O&M** > **Apsara Infrastructure Management**
> **Resources**. The **Product & Cluster O&M** page appears.

3. Enter `ascm-A` in the **Product | Cluster** search box on the **Product & Cluster O&M**
page, find the ascm-A-xxx cluster, and then click **Cluster Details** in the Actions column.
4. On the **cluster details** page, click the **Desired State Configuration** tab.
5. In the list of files displayed on the left, click **kv.conf** and click Display Content on the right.
Press Ctrl+F to search for `region` and `internet-domain` . Replace ${global:region} with the `region` value and ${global:internet-domain} with the `internet-domain` value.

**Method 2: Search for the endpoint in the Apsara Infrastructure**

**Management console**

OP to make API calls

**Procedure**

1. Enter `ascm-A` in the **Product | Cluster** search box on the **Product & Cluster O&M**
page, find the ascm-A-xxx cluster, and then click **Cluster Details** in the Actions column.
2. n the Services tab of the cluster details page, enter `ascm-brm` in the Service search box,
find the ascm-brm service, and then click **Details** in the Actions column.
3. On the service details page, click **Manage#** in the Components section. Then, click the
**Resources** tab in the Information of Component Manage# section.
4. Search for the resource named `ascm-aliyun-com-dns` , click the icon in the **Resource**
**Application Parameters** column to display detailed parameter settings, and then view
the value of **domain**.

### 2.2 Obtain an SDK of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

**Uni-manager Management Console**

To call API operations by using the Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP) gateway in the Apsara Unimanager Management Console, you must use an SDK. You can go to the page of Apsara Stack SDKs and download the package of the desired **SDK**
**core library** based on the programming language.

> **Note:** We recommend that you use an SDK for Java, Python, or Go. If you use SDKs for other programming languages, the SDKs may be incompatible with your system.

**Handle errors**

If an error occurs on the server or SDK when you use the SDK for Java, an error response is returned. The error response contains an error code and an error message. In most cases, you do not need to handle the errors returned by the SDK for Java. You need to only handle the errors returned by the server based on error messages. `ServerException` indicates a server error. `ClientException` indicates an SDK error. The following error indicates that the AccessKey ID is invalid. You must specify a valid AccessKey ID.

```
com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException: InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound : Specified access key is not found.
```

If you want to handle the SDK errors returned by the SDK, refer to the following example to write your code: OP to make API calls

```java
try {
    AcsResponse response = client.getAcsResponse(request);
    // Process the response.
    // ...
}catch (ServerException e){
    // Add your own computing logic for handling errors here.
    // For example, you can obtain the error information.
    System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode());
    System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg());
    // If you are unable to fix the error, submit a ticket and provide the request ID t
o Alibaba Cloud technical support.
    System.out.println("ResponseId=" + e.getRequestId());
}catch (ClientException e){
    // Add your own computing logic for handling errors here.
    // For example, you can obtain the error information.
    System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode());
    System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg());
```

`}`

The following error indicates that the AccessKey ID is invalid. You must specify a valid AccessKey ID.

```
aliyunsdkcore.acs\_exception.exceptions.ServerException: HTTP Status: 404 Error:InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound Specified access keey is not found.
```

If you want to handle the SDK errors returned by the SDK, refer to the following example to write your code:

```bash
try:
    response = client.do_action_with_exception(request)
except ServerException as e:
    # Add your own computing logic for handling errors here.
    # For example, you can obtain and display the error information.
    print e.get_http_status()
    print e.get_error_code()
    print e.get_error_msg()
```

###### 3.1.1.1.1 CreateOrganization

Creates an organization.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers and does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/organization/add HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| name | String | Body | Yes | ascm-test | The name of the organization. |
| parentId | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The parent organization ID. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query the ID. Note The ID of the root organization is 1. This parameter is required. |
| orgParentUuid | String | Body | No | org- 101bbf866a93 0ae6******** | The parent organization UUID. |
| orgUuid | String | Body | No | org- 101bbf866a93 0ae6******** | The organization UUID. The system automatically generates a value for this parameter. |

| multiCloudStat us | String | Body | No | null | The multi-cloud status of the organization. Default value: null. Valid values: master: The organization is a primary-cloud organization. slave: The organization is a secondary-cloud organization. null. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| extraInfo | String | Body | No | null | The additional information. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The status code. 200: The call is successful. 400: The organization name is left empty. The ID of the parent organization is left empty. The parent organization does not exist. The AccessKey pair is invalid. One or more parameters are invalid. 403: You do not have permissions. 500: A remote call error occurred. An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10s, the operation times out. |
| data | Struct |   | The data returned. |
| alias | String | test | The alias of the organization. The system automatically generates an alias that is the same name as the organization name. |
| ctime | Long | 1606791494471 | The time when the organization was created. |

| cuserId | String | admin | The username of the user who created the organization. |
|---|---|---|---|
| extraInfo | String | null | The additional information. |
| id | Integer | 1 | The organization ID. |
| internal | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the organization is a preset organization. Note The system automatically generates a preset organization, which is also named the default organization. |
| level | String | 0.1 | The level of the organization. Note The level of the root organization is 0, and the levels of level-1 organizations are 0.1. 1 in 0.1 indicates that the ID of the parent organization of level-1 organizations is 1. In this case, the parent organization is the root organization. All levels follow the same rule. For example, if the ID of a level-1 organization is 3, the level of its subordinate organization is 0.1.3. |
| mtime | Long | 1606791494471 | The time when the organization was last modified. Note In the scenario in which you create an organization, the system returns the same value for the mtime and ctime parameters. |
| multiCloudStat us | String | master | Indicates whether the organization is a multi-cloud organization. master: The organization is a primary- cloud organization. slave: The organization is a secondary- cloud organization. This parameter is returned only in multi- cloud scenarios. |
| muserId | String | admin | The username of the user who modified the organization. |

| name | String | test | The name of the organization. |
|---|---|---|---|
| parentId | Integer | 1 | The parent organization ID. Note The ID of the root organization is 1. |
| supportRegion List | List | ["cn-qingdao- env17-d01"] | The list of available regions. Note This parameter takes effect only for level-1 organizations. If a level-1 organization is created, the ID of the central region is returned for this parameter. If a level-2 organization or its subordinate organization is created, no value is returned for this parameter. |
| supportRegion s | String | cn-qingdao-****- d01 | The available regions. |
| uuid | String | 1231 | The organization UUID. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. Examples: success: The call is successful. Can't find user by specified accessKey: No user is found by using the AccessKey pair. Caller is not the parent of user: xxx: You do not have sufficient permissions. Calling manage returns empty body: No results are returned for the call. |
| pureListData | Boolean | true | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| redirect | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request is redirected. Valid values: true false |
| requestId | String | 16d09b14-8a59- ****-****- 7536fe897b66 | The request ID. |

###### 3.1.1.2.5 ListResourceGroup

Queries the list of resource sets that are visible to your account.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers and does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/resource_group/list_resource_group HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| resourceGroup Name | String | Body | No | test | The name of the resource set that you want to query. If you specify only the organizationId parameter, the system returns resource sets that belong to the organization and are visible to your account. If you specify only the resourceGroupName parameter, the system returns resource sets whose names contain the specified value and that are visible to your account. |
| organizationId | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The organization ID. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query organization IDs. Note Only resource sets in the specified organization are returned. Resource sets in the subordinate organizations of the specified organization are not returned. If you leave this parameter empty or set this parameter to 1, the system returns all resource sets that are visible to your account. |
| pageNumber | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
| pageSize | Integer | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Default value: 10. |

| data | Array of dataItem |   | The data returned. |
| creator | String | admin | The username of the user who created the resource set. |
| gmtCreated | Float | 1606719003858 | The time when the resource set was created. |
| id | Integer | 1 | The ID of the resource set. |

###### 3.1.1.3.6 SetDefaultRole

Sets a default role for a user. A user can have multiple roles. If a default role is set for a user, the default role is automatically used in the next logon of the user to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. After logon, the user can switch to a different role on the User Information page or the Home page.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/setDefaultRole HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginName | String | Body | No | testu | The logon name of the user. Note If this parameter is left empty, your logon name is used by default. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roleId | Integer | Body | Yes | 2 | The ID of the role. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query role IDs. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. 200: The request was successful. 403: You do not have permissions. 404: The user does not exist. The role does not exist. The user do not have the specified role. 500: An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |
| message | String | success | The message. success: The request was successful. Forbidden: You do not have permissions. NotExist: The user does not exist. The role does not exist. The user do not have the specified role. InternalServerError: An internal error occurred. |

| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. true false |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/setDefaultRole HTTP/1.1
```

`{`

```json
    "loginName": "testu",
    "roleId": 2
```

`}` Sample success responses `XML` format

```xml
<redirect>false</redirect> <cost>10000</cost> <code>200</code> <success>true</success> <message>success</message>
```

`JSON` format `{`

```json
    "cost": 10000,
    "code": 200,
    "success": true,
    "message": "success"
```

###### 3.1.1.4.2 AddUser

Creates a user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/addUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | Yes | testuser2022 | The logon name of the user. It must be 2 to 64 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, underscores ( ), hyphens _ (-), and periods (.) Note This parameter is required. |

| displayName | String | Body | Yes | testuser2022 | The display name of the user. It must be 1 to 128 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, hyphens (-), periods (.), and at signs (@). Note This parameter is required. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| email | String | Body | Yes | test@example .com | The email address of the user. Note This parameter is required. |
| loginPolicyId | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The ID of the logon policy that needs to be used for the user. You can call the ListLoginPolicies operation to query the ID of the logon policy. Note If you do not specify this parameter, the default policy is used. |
| organizationId | Integer | Body | Yes | 60 | The ID of the organization to which the user belongs. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query the organization ID. Note This parameter is required. |
| mobileNationC ode | String | Body | Yes | 86 | The country code that is added to the mobile phone number of the user. Note This parameter is required. |
| cellphoneNum | String | Body | Yes | 188****8888 | The mobile number of the user. Note This parameter is required. |

| roleIdList | Repeat List | Body | No | [2,4] | The IDs of roles. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query the IDs of roles. Note If you do not specify a role when you create a user, the resource user role is assigned to the user by default. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| organizationUu id | String | Body | No | lg-123456789 | The UUID of the organization. You can call the GetOrganization operation to query the UUID of the organization. |
| telephoneNum | String | Body | No | 11111111 | The landline number of the user. |
| dingTalkToken | String | Body | No | zxcvbnm | The DingTalk key. Note It is the signature key of the DingTalk chatbot that you specify when you create the user. |
| enableDingTal k | Boolea n | Body | No | false | Specifies whether to enable notification by using DingTalk. |
| enableShortMe ssage | Boolea n | Body | No | false | Specifies whether to enable notification by using text messages. |
| enableEmail | Boolea n | Body | No | false | Specifies whether to enable notification by using emails. |
| multiCloudStat us | String | Body | No | null | Specifies whether the user is a multi-cloud user. Default value: null. Valid values: master slave null |

###### 3.1.1.4.3 DeactivateUser

Deactivates a user. If you deactivate a user, all AccessKey pairs of the user are automatically disabled. Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition V3.12.0 SP016 or later supports this operation. Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition V3.14.0 SP013 or later supports this operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/deactivateUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | Yes | testuser2022 | The logon name of the user. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. 200: The request was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: Access to a resource is prohibited. 404: The requested resource does not exist. 406: The account is not activated. 409: The resource already exists. 418: Code-based verification failed. 419: Third-party service authentication failed. 420: Signature verification failed. 421: Certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey ID does not have permissions to perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey ID does not exist or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal service error occurred. 511: The value of a parameter exceeds the defined threshold. 512: The security token issued by STS has become invalid. 513: The dependent service is abnormal. |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost | Integer | 118 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |
| data | Struct |   | The information about the user. |
| accessKeys | Array of accessKey |   | The AccessKey pairs. Note Only the administrator can obtain the AccessKey pairs of a preset user. |
| accessKey |   |   |   |
| accesskeyId | String | tCr5mJhpjo****** | The AccessKey ID. |

| ctime | Long | 1606675230000 | The time when the AccessKey pair was created. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| cuserId | String | admin | The ID of the user who created the AccessKey pair. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| id | Integer | 1 | The primary key of the AccessKey pair. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| region | String | cn-qingdao-****- d01 | The region in which the AccessKey pair is available. |
| status | String | ACTIVE | The status of the AccessKey pair. ACTIVE: The AccessKey pair is enabled. INACTIVE: The AccessKey pair is disabled. |
| cellphoneNum | String | 188****8888 | The mobile number of the user. |
| default | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the user is a preset user. Note A user that is automatically created during initialization is a preset user. If the user is a custom user, the value of this field is false. |
| defaultRole | Struct |   | The default role. Note The default role is automatically selected as the current role after the user logs on. |

###### 3.1.1.4.4 GetUserInfo

Queries user information.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/getUserInfo HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | No | testuser2022 | The logon name of the user. Note The loginName parameter takes precedence over the userAccessKeyId and pk parameters. If you specify a logon name that does not exist, the system returns an error that indicates the user does not exist. |
| userAccessKey Id | String | Body | No | UyAna7V7RG* ***** | The AccessKey ID of the user. Note If you do not specify the loginName parameter, you can leave the loginName parameter empty. If neither of the longinName and userAccessKeyId parameters is specified, the operation is performed based on the pk parameter. |

| pk | String | Body | No | 25925866254 4****** | The primary key of the account. Note If only the pk parameter is specified, the operation is performed based on the pk parameter. If the loginName or userAccessKeyId parameter is specified, you can leave the pk parameter empty. If none of the request parameters are specified, an error is returned. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

###### 3.1.1.4.5 ListAccessKeysForManagedUsers

Queries AccessKey information of all users that are managed by the current user. You can use the OrganizationId and LoginName parameters to specify the organization and users that you want to query. If you do not configure the parameters, the AccessKey information of all users that are managed by the user who calls this operation is returned. If you specify the organization and users, users whose AccessKey information is returned are also managed by the user who calls this operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /user/accesskey/listAccessKeysForManagedUsers HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| LoginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | test | The username. |
| PageNum | Integ er | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. Pages start from page 1. |
| PageSize | Integ er | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Default value: 10. Maximum value: 100. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| data | Array |   | The returned AccessKey information. |

| --status | String | ACTIVE | The status of the AccessKey pair. ACTIVE: The AccessKey pair is enabled. INACTIVE: The AccessKey pair is disabled. |
| -loginName | String | testuser | The logon name of the user. |
| -primaryKey | String | 25925468**** | The primary key of the Resource Access Management (RAM) user, which is used as the unique identifier of the account. |

###### 3.1.1.4.9 ListUsersInsideRole

Queries all users that are associated with a role.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/listUsersInsideRole HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| organizationId | Integer | Body | No | 3 | The ID of the organization under which you want to query users that are associated with a role. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query organization IDs. Note You can ignore this parameter. |
| currentPage | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
| pageSize | Integer | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. |
| loginName | String | Body | No | test | The SQL regular expression for logon names of the users. Note If you specify this parameter, users that are associated with the role and meet the specified regular expression condition are returned. If you do not specify this parameter, all users that are associated with the role are returned. |
| roleId | Integer | Body | Yes | 1 | The ID of the role. You can call the ListRoles operation to query role IDs. |

###### 3.1.1.4.10 LockUser

Locks a specific user. After you lock a user, you cannot modify the attributes of the user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/lockUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | Integ er | Body | No | 3 | The user ID. You need to configure either loginName or id to specify the user that you want to lock. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user. You need to configure either loginName or id to specify the user that you want to lock. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| cost | Integer | 1000 | The amount of time that is consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/lockUser HTTP/1.1
```

###### 3.1.1.4.11 ModifyUserInformation

Modifies the information about a specified system or historical user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the Common parameters topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/modifyUserInformation HTTP/1.1
```

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | Body | No | 5817 | The user ID. If you specify loginName, this parameter is optional. Note If both id and loginName are specified, the id parameter has a higher priority. You can call the ListUsers operation to query the ID of a system user. You can call the ListDeletedUsers operation to query the ID of a historical user. |
| loginName | String | Body | No | testuser2022 | The new name of the user. If you specify id, this parameter is optional. Note If both id and loginName are specified, the id parameter has a higher priority. |
| displayName | String | Body | No | testuser2022 | The new display name of the user. It must be 1 to 128 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, hyphens (- ), periods (.), and at signs (@). |

| loginPolicyId | Integer | Body | No | 1084 | The ID of the new logon policy with which the user is associated. You can call the ListLoginPolicies operation to query the ID of the logon policy. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mobileNationC ode | String | Body | No | 86 | The new country code that is added to the mobile phone number of the user. |
| cellphoneNum | String | Body | No | 188****8888 | The new mobile phone number of the user. |
| telephoneNum | String | Body | No | 12345678 | The new landline number of the user. |
| email | String | Body | No | test@example .com | The new email address of the user. |
| description | String | Body | No | test data | The new description of the user. |
| dingTalkToken | String | Body | No | 17762sdsa | The new DingTalk key. Note It is the signature key of the DingTalk chatbot that you specify when you create the user. |
| enableDingTal k | Boolea n | Body | No | true | Specifies whether notifications by using DingTalk are enabled. |
| enableShortMe ssage | Boolea n | Body | No | true | Specifies whether notifications by using text messages are enabled. |
| enableEmail | Boolea n | Body | No | true | Specifies whether notifications by using emails are enabled. |
| multiCloudStat us | String | Body | No | slave | The multi-cloud synchronization status of the user. Default value: null. Valid values: master slave null |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The returned HTTP status code. 200: The call is successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: The operation is prohibited. Access to a specific resource is prohibited. 404: The resource that you want to access does not exist. 406: The account is not activated. 409: The resource that you want to save or add already exists. 418: The verification based on a verification code failed. 419: The third-party service authentication failed. 420: The signature verification failed. 421: The certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey pair is valid. ###### 3.1.1.4.13 RelateSystemWithUser

Associates the specified user with an external system.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/relateSystemWithUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | Integ er | Body | No | 3 | The ID of the user. You must specify the user that you want to associate with the external system by configuring one of the id and loginName parameters in the request. |
| loginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user. You must specify the user that you want to associate with the external system by configuring one of the id and loginName parameters in the request. |
| relativeSy stem | Strin g | Body | No | cmp | The name of the external system with which you want to associate the user. If you do not specify this parameter in a RelateSystemWithUser request, all association records of the user with external systems are cleared. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The returned HTTP status code. |
| cost | Integer | 1000 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/relateSystemWithUser HTTP/1.1
```

`{`

```json
    "id":3,
    "relativeSystem": "cmp"
```

`}` Sample success responses `JSON` format `{`

```json
 "code":"200",
 "cost":1000,
 "success":true,
 "message":"success"
```

`}` `XML` format

```xml
<code>200</code> <cost>1000</cost> <success>true</success> <message>success</message>
```

###### 3.1.1.4.14 RemoveRoleFromUser

Removes a role from the specified user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/removeRoleFromUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user from which you want to remove a role. This parameter must be specified in the request. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roleId | Integ er | Body | No | 6 | The ID of the role that you want to remove from the user. This parameter must be specified in the request. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The returned HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The request was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: The operation is prohibited. Access to a specific resource is prohibited. 404: The resource that you want to access does not exist. 406: The account is not activated. 409: The resource that you want to save or add already exists. 418: The verification based on a verification code failed. 419: The third-party service authentication failed. 420: The signature verification failed. 421: The certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey pair is valid. However, the user to whom the AccessKey pair belongs cannot perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey pair is invalid, does not exist, or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal error occurred. This code is returned if an unidentified exception occurred. 511: The parameter value exceeds the defined threshold. 512: The security token issued by STS becomes invalid. 513: The dependent service is abnormal. |

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost | Integer | 1022 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only the list data is returned. This parameter is no longer used. |
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/removeRoleFromUser HTTP/1.1
```

```json
    "loginName":"testuser"
```

###### 3.1.1.4.15 RemoveUserByLoginName

Deletes a user. A deleted user is added to the user history. You can call the RecoverUserByLoginName operation to recover a deleted user.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers and does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the Common parameters topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/removeUserByLoginName HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

###### 3.1.1.4.16 ResetPasswordByLoginName

Resets the password of a user. Only administrators of an organization can reset the password of a user in the organization. The ResetPasswordByLoginName operation resets the password of a user to a random password. You can perform the following steps to view the random password in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console: Click Enterprise in the top navigation bar. In the leftside navigation pane, choose Users > Users. Find the user whose password you have reset, and choose ... > View User Information in the Actions column. Click the eye icon next to the Password field. When the user uses the random password to log on for the first time, the user is required to change the random password. If you use Enterprise Edition v3.17.0 or later, we recommend that you use ResetUserPasswordByLoginName instead of ResetPasswordByLoginName.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers and does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the Common parameters topic.


| cost | Integer | 10000 | The time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |
| message | String | success | The message. success: The request was successful. Forbidden: You do not have permissions. NotExist: The user does not exist. InternalServerError: An internal error occurred. |

| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. true false |

**Examples**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/resetPasswordByLoginName HTTP/1.1 Common request headers
```

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers and does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/removeResourceSetFromUserGroup HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| userGroupId | Integer | Body | Yes | 1 | The user group ID. You can call the ListUserGroups operation to query user group IDs. |
| resourceSetId | Integer | Body | Yes | 1 | The resource set ID. You can call the ListResourceGroup operation to query resource set IDs. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. 200: The request was successful. 400: One or more parameters are not specified. 403: You do not have permissions. 404: The user group or resource set does not exist. 500: An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |

| message | String | success | The message. success: The request was successful. InvalidParameter: One or more parameters are not specified. Forbidden: You do not have permissions. NotExist: The user group or resource set does not exist. InternalServerError: An internal error occurred. |
|---|---|---|---|
| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. true false |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/removeResourceSetFromUserGroup HTTP/1.1 Common request headers
```

| time | Long | Body | No | 16624468634 45 | The logon timestamp. The default value is the current timestamp of the system. |

For example, if the user is associated with a logon IP address blacklist policy, and the logon IP address is on the blacklist, the value of the data parameter is false. |

##### 3.1.2.5 GetEnterpriseCenterQuota

Queries the quota limits in the enterprise center. The enterprise center allows you to query 12 quota limits. After the call is successful, information about the quota limits and the maximum values of metrics on the cloud platform is returned. MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be associated with a resource set. MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that can be associated with a resource set. MaxUserGroupCanJoinUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be added to a user group. MaxUserAddUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that a user can be added to. MaxUserAddResourceSetLimit: the maximum number of resource sets that a role of a user can be added to. MaxUserGroupAddResourceLimit: the maximum number of resource sets that a user group can be added to. MaxRoleBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be associated with a user. MaxRoleAuthorizationBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be associated with a user. MaxRoleBindAscmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be associated with a user group. MaxPolicyLimit: the maximum number of custom policies that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account. MaxRamGroupLimit: the maximum number of RAM groups that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account. MaxRamRoleLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/stat/enterpriseCenterQuota HTTP/1.1
```

This operation does not have operation-specific request parameters.

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| data | Normal | [{"current": 35,"displayName": "\u8d44\u6e90\u96 c6\u7ed1\u5b9a\u7 684\u6700\u5927\ u7528\u6237\u4e2 a\u6570","hasDetai l": true,"item": "MaxResourceSetBi ndAscmUserLimit", "quota": 10000,"updateTim e": 1692013092000}] | 12 quota limits are returned in a list, which contains the following fields: item: the limit item. current: the actual maximum value of the current item. displayName: the display field. hasDetail: indicates whether details are shown. quota: the quota of the limit item. updateTime: the timestamp of the last update. |
| dynamicMessa ge | String | [] | The dynamic prompt information. |
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| cost | Integer | 150 | The amount of time that is consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| successRespo nse | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the response is successful. |

##### 3.1.2.6 GetEnterpriseCenterQuotaDetail

Queries the detailed information about the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that have exceeded the preset enterprise quota or the specified quantity limits. You can call this operation to query the detailed information about the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that have exceeded the specified quota in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger or the quantity limits you specified in the request parameters.

**Request headers**

The SetIdPConfig operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/stat/enterpriseCenterQuotaDetail HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| type | Strin g | Body | No | MaxResourceSetBindAsc mUserLimit | The quota items in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger: MaxResourceSetBindAs cmUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be bound to a resource set. MaxResourceSetBindAs cmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that can be bound to a resource set. MaxUserGroupCanJoin UserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be added to a user group. MaxUserAddUserGroup Limit: the maximum number of user groups that a user can join. MaxUserAddResourceS etLimit: the maximum number of resource sets to which a user- specified role can be bound. MaxUserGroupAddReso urceLimit: the maximum number of resource sets to which a user group can be bound. MaxRoleBindAscmUser Limit: the maximum number of roles that can be bound to a user. MaxRoleAuthorizationB indAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of authorized RAM roles that can be bound to a user. MaxRoleBindAscmUser GroupLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be bound to a user group. |

|   |   |   |   |   | MaxPolicyLimit: the maximum number of custom policies that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. MaxRamGroupLimit: the maximum number of RAM groups that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. MaxRamRoleLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| limit | Integ er | Body | No | 100 | The quantity limits for the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that you want to query. If you leave this parameter empty, users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that exceed the specified quota in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger will be returned. |
| currentPag e | Integ er | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
| pageSize | Integ er | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 500. Default value: 10. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| data | Normal | [{"active":true,"co unt":13,"id":40617, "loginName":"ramu seriiiz","updateTim e":1692013097000 ,"username":"ramu seriiiz"}] | The returned data based on the value you specified for the type parameter. For more information, see the "Supplementary details of the data parameter" section of this topic. |

| dynamicMessa ge | String | [] | The dynamic prompt information. |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The response code. |
| cost | Integer | 17 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | "success" | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true and false. |
| successRespo nse | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true and false. |
| pageInfo | Struct |   | The pagination information. |
| -currentPage | Integer | 1 | The page number. |
| -pageSize | Integer | 10 | The number of entries per page. |
| -total | Integer | 9629 | The total number of entries returned. |
| -totalPage | Integer | 963 | The total number of pages returned. |

**Supplementary details of the data parameter**

If you set the type parameter to MaxUserAddUserGroupLimit, MaxUserAddResourceSetLimit, MaxRoleBindAscmUserLimit, or MaxRoleAuthorizationBindAscmUserLimit, the details of the user (UserEntry) type are returned. The details contain the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The user ID. |
| username | String | The display name of the user. |
| loginName | String | The logon name of the user. |
| isActive | Boolean | Indicates whether the user is active. |

| roleId | Integer | The default role ID. |
|---|---|---|
| roleName | String | The default role name. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxUserGroupCanJoinUserLimit, MaxUserGroupAddResourceLimit, or MaxRoleBindAscmUserGroupLimit, the details of the user group (UserGroupEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The ID of the user group. |
| augId | String | The UUID of the user group. |
| groupName | String | The name of the user group. |
| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the user group belongs. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserLimit or MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserGroupLimit, the details of the resource set (ResourceSetEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The ID of the resource set. |
| rsId | String | The UUID of the resource set. |
| resourceGroupName | String | The name of a resource set. |

| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the resource set belongs. |
|---|---|---|
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxPolicyLimit, MaxRamGroupLimit, or MaxRamRoleLimit, the details of the Apsara Stack tenant account (RamEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| aliyunId | Integer | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| accountKp | String | The primary key of the Apsara Stack tenant account. The primary key is used as the UID of the account. |
| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the Apsara Stack tenant account belongs. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

##### 3.1.3.3 DescribeSeriesIdFamilies

Queries instance families of PolarDB-X 1.0.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/manage/saleconf/drdsSpec/describeSeriesIdFamilies HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| resourceType | String | Body | No | DRDS | The resource type. Set the value to DRDS. Note This parameter is of the enumeration type and is case-sensitive. This parameter must be set to DRDS. If this parameter is set to another value, no data is returned. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| status | String | Body | No | Available | The status of the instance specifications. Valid values: Available Unavailable If the status of a specification is Unavailable, you cannot create PolarDB-X instances of the specification. |
| label | String | Body | No | true | Specifies whether to return the name of the instance families. Default value: false. Valid values: true false |

> **Note:** If none of these parameters are specified, all PolarDB-X 1.0 instance families are returned.

**Response parameters**

**code**: the HTTP status code. Type: string.
200: The request was successful. 500: The request failed.
**data**: the data returned. Type: string.
**creator**: the name of the user who created the instance. Type: string.
**gmtModified**: the time when the instance was created. Type: float.
**seriesName**: the name of the instance family. Type: string.
**modifier**: the user who last modified the instance. Type: string.
**orderBy**: the sorting order. By default, the results are sorted in ascending order by data
ID. This parameter can be ignored. Type: string.
**pageSize**: the number of pages. Type: integer.
**gmtCreate**: the name of the user who created the instance family. This is a virtual
parameter. This parameter can be ignored. Type: string.
**seriesId**: the ID of the instance family. Type: string.
**deleted**: indicates whether the specification is deleted. Type: boolean. Values:
false true
**pageOrder**: the page sorting order. The results are arranged in ascending order. Type:
string.
**isDeleted**: indicates whether the specification is deleted. Type: string. Values: N and Y. N
indicates that the specification is not deleted. Y indicates that the specification is deleted.
**pageSort**: the sorting field. This parameter can be ignored. Type: string.
**pageStart**: the page number. Pages start from 0. Type: integer.
**seriesNameLabel**: the name of the instance family. Type: string.
**resourceType**: the resource type. The value of this parameter is DRDS. Type: string.
**httpOk**: indicates whether an HTTP request is sent. The value of this parameter is false.
Type: boolean.
**success**: indicates whether the request was successful. Type: boolean.
true false
**message**: the message. If the request was successful, the value of this parameter is
describeSeriesIdFamilies success. If the request failed, an error message is returned. Type: string.

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/manage/saleconf/drdsSpec/describeSeriesIdFamilies HTTP/1.1 Common request headers
```

```json
    "status":"Available"
```

##### 3.1.3.7 UpdateInstanceBelong

Changes the resource set of an instance. You cannot change the resource set of an instance across level-1 organizations. When you call this operation, the system checks whether the quota limits of resource sets and instances are reached. If so, the error code 510 is returned. The security groups of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances and the vSwitches in the virtual private clouds (VPCs) can be changed only within the sharing scope of the VPC to which they belong. If you change the resource set of an ECS instance, the disks, snapshots, and elastic network interfaces (ENIs) of the ECS instance are also changed. If you change the resource set of a VPC, the route tables in the VPC are also changed.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the Common parameters topic.

You cannot change the resource set of an instance across level-1 organizations. Change failed. 403: You do not have permissions. 510: The quota limit is reached. |

#### 3.1.4 Configurations

##### 3.1.4.1 BatchCreateRAMServiceRole

Creates multiple service-linked roles at a time. You can call the ListRAMServiceRoles operation to query created service-linked roles. A service-linked role is used by a trusted Alibaba Cloud service to access other Alibaba Cloud services or manage resources in other Alibaba Cloud services. If you create an instance of an Alibaba Cloud service that needs access to another Alibaba Cloud service, a service-linked role is automatically created for the service in the level-1 organization of the organization in which you create the instance. For example, an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance needs the permissions to create an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket for image storage. The ECS instance needs to assume the corresponding service-linked role that is provided by OSS. This way, the ECS instance is granted permissions to manage OSS resources.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```

```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| organizationId List.N | Repeat List | Body | Yes | ["14","18","19" ,"21","23","24" ] | The organization IDs. Separate multiple organization IDs with commas (,). You can call the GetOrganizationTree operation to query organization IDs. |
| productName | String | Body | Yes | NAS | The name of the service. You can call the ListRAMServiceRoleProducts operation to query service names. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. 200: The request was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: Access to a resource is prohibited. 404: The requested resource does not exist. 406: The account is not activated. 409: The resource already exists. 418: Code-based verification failed. 419: Third-party service authentication failed. 420: Signature verification failed. 421: Certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey ID does not have permissions to perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey ID does not exist or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal service error occurred. 511: The value of a parameter exceeds the defined threshold. 512: The security token issued by STS has become invalid. 513: The dependent service is abnormal. |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost | Integer | 22 | The time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |
| message | String | success | The message. Note This parameter is returned, regardless of whether the request was successful. If the request was successful, success is returned as the value of this parameter. If the request failed, a custom error message or an error message in the error stack is returned. |

| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. Note This parameter is deprecated. true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. true false |

**Examples**

##### 3.1.4.8 ResetPasswordPolicy

Resets the current password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. After you call this operation, the password policy is reset to the default password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. To modify the password policy of the Apsara Unimanager Management Console, call the SetPasswordPolicy operation. For information about the default password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, see the response data.

**Request header**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/resetPasswordPolicy HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

None

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The status code returned. 200: The call is successful. 500: An internal error occurred. 500 is returned if an unidentified exception occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 14 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. Note If the time consumed from the request to the response of an operation called by using ASAPI exceeds 10 seconds, the operation times out. |
| data | Struct |   | The information about the password policy. |

| hardExpiry | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password has a validity period. true: The password expires. After the expiration date, the user cannot log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. false: The password does not expire. Note You can use the maxPasswordAge parameter to learn the password validity period. You need to update the password at the earliest opportunity before the validity period ends. If the password has expired, you need to contact the operations administrator or platform administrator to reset the password. |
|---|---|---|---|
| maxLoginAtte mps | Integer | 5 | The maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. Note Valid values: 0 to 32. |
| maxPassword Age | Integer | 90 | The validity period of the password. Unit: days. 0 indicates that the password expiration policy is not enabled. Note Valid values: 0 to 1095. |
| minimumPass wordLength | Integer | 10 | The minimum number of characters in a password. Note Valid values: 8 to 32. |
| passwordError CaptchaTime | Integer | 3 | The number of logon attempts with an incorrect password for triggering CAPTCHA verification. |
| passwordError LockPeriod | Integer | 30 | The duration for which the account is frozen. Unit: minutes. Note If the maximum number of attempts is reached, the account enters the frozen state. During this period, you cannot log on by using the account. Valid values: 0 to 1440. |

| passwordError TolerancePerio d | Integer | 5 | The password error tolerance period. The default value is 60 minutes. This indicates that N times of logon attempts with an incorrect password are allowed in 60 minutes. The maxLoginAttemps parameter specifies the maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. |
|---|---|---|---|
| passwordReus ePrevention | Integer | 5 | The number of previous passwords that a user is prevented from using. Default value: 0. The default value indicates that the user can use previous passwords. Note Valid values: 0 to 24. |
| requireLowerc aseCharacters | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain lowercase letters. |
| requireNumbe rs | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain digits. |
| requireSymbol s | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain special characters. |
| requireUpperc aseCharacters | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain uppercase letters. |
| message | String | success | The error message. Note The error message is returned no matter whether the call is successful or failed. In most cases, success is returned if the call is successful, and a custom message or the error message of an exception is returned if the call failed. |
| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data is returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |

| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request is redirected. true: The request is redirected. false: The request is not redirected. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. true false |

##### 3.1.5.1 Computing

###### 3.1.5.1.1 E-HPC

After you call the MeteringQuery operation to query statistical data, common response parameters and service-specific response parameters are returned. This topic describes the response parameters specific to Elastic High Performance Computing (E-HPC).

| Parameter | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Pos | Primary key | The primary key consists of the service ID, organization ID, and the beginning of the time range that you want to query. |
| OrgName | Organization name | The name of the organization to which the cluster belongs. |
| ResourceGId | Resource set ID | The ID of the resource set to which the cluster belongs. |

| ResourceGName | Resource set name | The name of the resource set to which the cluster belongs. |
|---|---|---|

| RegionId | Region ID | The region ID. |
| StartTime | Start time | The beginning of the time range queried. The time is displayed in UTC. |
| EndTime | End time | The end of the time range queried. The time is displayed in UTC. |

| Name | Cluster name | The cluster name. |
| Status | Cluster status | The status of the E-HPC cluster. Valid values: uninit: The cluster is not initialized. creating: The cluster is being created. init: The cluster is being initialized. running: The cluster is running. exception: The cluster encounters an exception. releasing: The cluster is being released. |

| InstanceType | Compute node type | The instance type of the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance that serves as a compute node of the E-HPC cluster. Example: ecs.e4v2.xlarge. Note For more information about the supported instance types, see ECS instance families and instance types. |
|---|---|---|
| Count | Number of compute nodes | The number of compute nodes. Valid values: 1 to 99. |
| ClusterSumCoreTime | vCPU-hour quota | The vCPU-hour quota of the cluster. Note vCPU-hours = Number of vCPUs × Hours. Unit: hours. |
| ClusterUsedCoreTime | Spent vCPU-hours | The spent vCPU-hours of the cluster. Note vCPU-hours = Number of vCPUs × Hours. Unit: hours. |

| OsTag | Operating system | The operating system of the cluster. |
