## 4 Cloud Monitor Service API Reference

**Reference**

### 4.1 API Reference

#### 4.1.1 Monitoring data on time series metrics of cloud services

**of cloud services**

##### 4.1.1.1 DescribeMetricLast

Queries the most recent monitoring data of a monitored object.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeMetricL ast | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeMetricLast. |
| MetricName | String | Yes | CPUUtilization | The metric name. |
| Namespace | String | Yes | acs ecs dashbo _ _ ard | The namespace of the service. Specify the value in the format of acs Service name. _ |

| Dimensions | String | No | [{"instanceId":" XXXXXX"}] | The dimension map of the monitored resources. Set the value to a collection of key- value pairs. A typical key-value pair is instanceId:XXXXXX . The key and value can each be 1 to 64 bytes in length. Values that contain more than 64 characters will be truncated. Values of key and value can contain letters, digits, periods (.), hyphens (-), underscores ( ), forward slashes (/), and _ backslashes (\). Note If you set Dimensions to ordered strings in the request, the value of this parameter is a key-value map expressed in JSON strings. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EndTime | String | No | 2019-01-31 10:10:00 | The end of the time range to query. This value is a UNIX timestamp that represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. Note Only a time range within the last 270 days can be specified to query. |
| Express | String | No | {"groupby": ["userId","instan ceId"]} | The expression that is used to calculate the query results in real time. |
| Length | String | No | 1000 | The number of entries per page. Default value: 1000. |

| NextToken | String | No | 1576143285000 9dd70bb64cff1f 0fff6c0b08ffff07 3be5fb1e785e2 b020f7fed9b5e1 37bd810a6d6cff 5ae**** | The pagination token. If the number of results exceeds the maximum number of entries allowed on a single page, a pagination token is returned. This pagination token can be used as an input parameter to obtain entries on the next page. If a response does not contain pagination tokens, all query results are returned. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Period | String | No | 60 | The time interval at which to query monitoring data. Typically, the time interval is the same as the interval for reporting metric data. Unit: seconds. If you do not specify this parameter, raw data is queried at the reporting interval specified when the corresponding metric was created. If a statistical period was specified for the corresponding alert rule, raw data is queried based on the statistical period. |
| StartTime | String | No | 2019-01-31 10:00:00 | The beginning of the time range to query. This value is a UNIX timestamp that represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. Note Only a time range that covers a maximum of 31 days within the last 270 days can be specified to query. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| RequestId | String | 021472A6-25E3- 4094-8D00- BA4B6A5486C3 | The request ID. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Note The HTTP status code 200 indicates that the request succeeds. |
| Success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| Period | String | 60 | The time interval at which monitoring data was queried. Unit: seconds. |
| NextToken | String | xxxxxx | The pagination token. |
| Datapoints | String | [{"timestamp":154 8777660000,"userI d":"123","instanceI d":"i- abc","Minimum":9. 92,"Average":9.92, "Maximum":9.92}] | The monitoring data. |
| Message | String | Success | The error message returned if the operation fails. |

##### 4.1.1.2 DescribeMetricList

Queries the monitoring data of a time series metric for a cloud service within a specified period of time. For more information about the values of parameters such as Namespace, Metric, Period, and Dimensions for each cloud service, see Appendix 1: Metrics.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeMetricLi st | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeMetricList. |
| MetricName | String | Yes | cpu idle _ | The metric name. |
| Namespace | String | Yes | acs ecs dashbo _ _ ard | The namespace of the service. Format: acs service name. _ |

| Dimensions | String | No | [{"instanceId": "i- abcdefgh12****" }] | The dimensions that specify the resources whose monitoring data you want to query. Set the value to a collection of key-value pairs. A typical collection of key-value pairs is in the instanceId:XXXXXX format. The key and value can each be 1 to 64 bytes in length. Values that contain more than 64 characters are truncated. Values of key and value can contain letters, digits, periods (.), hyphens (-), underscores ( ), forward slashes (/), and _ backslashes (\). Note Dimensions must be formatted as a JSON string in a specific order. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EndTime | String | No | 2019-01-30 00:10:00 | The end time. The following formats are supported: UNIX timestamp: the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 Thursday, January 1, 1970. UTC time: the UTC time that follows the YYYY-MM- DDThh:mm:ssZ format. |
| Express | String | No | {"groupby": ["userId","instan ceId"]} | The expression that is used to compute the query results in real time. Only the groupby expression is supported. This expression is similar to the groupby statement that is used in databases. |
| Length | String | No | 1000 | The number of entries per page. Default value: 1000. |

| NextToken | String | No | 1576148535000 9dd70bb64cff1f 0fff750b08ffff07 3be5fb1e785e2 b020f1a949d5e a14aea7fed82f0 1dd87311 | The pagination token. Note You do not need to specify this parameter if you only want to obtain entries on the first page. The pagination token returned in a response can be used as an input parameter for obtaining entries on the next page. If a response contains no pagination tokens, all query results have been returned. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Period | String | No | 60 | The time interval at which monitoring data was queried. Unit: seconds. Valid values: 60, 300, and 900, which represent 1 minute, 5 minutes, and 15 minutes, respectively. Note Configure this parameter based on your business requirements. For example, if you set this parameter to 60, only 1,000 records are returned, though a total of 1,440 records are generated. This is because the maximum number of records that can be returned for each query is 1,000. If you set this parameter to 300, 288 records are returned. |
| StartTime | String | No | 2019-01-30 00:00:00 | The start time. The following formats are supported: UNIX timestamp: the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 Thursday, January 1, 1970. UTC time: the UTC time that follows the YYYY-MM- DDThh:mm:ssZ format. Note The period specified by StartTime and EndTime includes the time point specified by EndTime but does not include the time point specified by StartTime. StartTime must be earlier than EndTime. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 3121AE7D-4AFF- 4C25-8F1D- C8226EBB1F42 | The request ID. |
| Code | String | 200 | The response code. Note The status code 200 indicates that the request was successful. |
| Success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| NextToken | String | 15761441850009d d70bb64cff1f0fff6d 0b08ffff073be5fb1 e785e2b020f7fed9 b5e137bd810a6d6 cff5aee816 | The pagination token. Note You do not need to specify this parameter if you only want to obtain entries on the first page. The pagination token returned in a response can be used as an input parameter for obtaining entries on the next page. If a response contains no pagination tokens, all query results have been returned. |
| Period | String | 60 | The time interval at which monitoring data was queried. Unit: seconds. Valid values: 60, 300, and 900. |
| Datapoints | String | [{"timestamp":154 8777660000,"userI d":"123","instanceI d":"i- abc","Minimum":9. 92,"Average":9.92, "Maximum":9.92}] | The monitoring data. |
| Message | String | Success | The returned message. |

**Examples**

```
http(s)://[Endpoint]/?Action=DescribeMetricList &MetricName=cpu_idle &Namespace=acs_ecs_dashboard &<Common request parameters>
```

##### 4.1.1.3 DescribeMetricMetaList

Queries the descriptions of time series metrics that are supported by CloudMonitor. This operation is used together with DescribeMetricList or DescribeMetricLast.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeMetricM etaList | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeMetricMetaList. |
| Namespace | String | Yes | acs kvstore _ | The namespace of the monitored service. You can call the DescribeProjectMeta operation to query the namespace of each service. |

|   |   |   |   |   |   | The tags of the metric. Specify the tags in the following format: [{"name":"Tag |   |   |

|   |   |   |   |   |   | value"}] |   |   |
| Labels |   | String | No | [{"name":"prod uctCategory","v alue":"kvstore o _ ld"}] |   |   |   |   |
| MetricName |   | String | No | CPUUtilization |   | The name of the metric. The metric with the specified name is matched. |   |   |
| PageNumber |   | Integer | No | 1 |   | The page number. Default value: 1. |   |   |
| PageSize |   | Integer | No | 30 |   | The number of entries per page. Default value: 30. |   |   |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| Resource |   |   |   | The information about a metric found. |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Dimensions | String |   | instanceId | The dimensions of the metric. Multiple dimensions are separated by commas (,). |   |   |
| Labels | String |   |   | The tags of the metric. The value is a JSON string in the following format: [{"name":"Tag name","value":"Tag value"}] . The string can include repeated tag names. The following tag names are available: metricCategory: the category of the metric. alertEnable: indicates whether the alert is enabled. alertUnit: the unit of the metric in the alert. unitFactor: the factor for metric unit conversion. minAlertPeriod: the minimum interval at which the alert is reported. productCategory: the category of the service. |   |   |

| TotalCount | String |   | 12 | The total number of entries returned. |   |   |

##### 4.1.1.5 DescribeMetricData

Queries the monitoring data of a metric for a specified cloud service.

**Request header**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Locati on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Parame ter | Typ e | Locati on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Namespac e | Strin g | Query | Yes | acs ecs dashboard _ _ | The namespace of the cloud service. For more information about the namespaces of cloud services, see Appendix 1: Metrics. |
| MetricNa me | Strin g | Query | Yes | cpu idle _ | The metric that is used to monitor the cloud service. For more information about the metrics of cloud services, see Appendix 1: Metrics. |
| Period | Strin g | Query | No | 60 | The statistical period of the metric. Valid values: 15, 60, 900, and 3600. Unit: seconds. If this parameter is not specified, monitoring data is queried based on the period in which metric values are reported. For more information about the statistical period of a metric that is specified by the MetricName parameter, see Appendix 1: Metrics. |
|   |   |   |   |   | The start of the time range to query monitoring data. If the StartTime and EndTime parameters are not specified, the monitoring data of the last statistical period is queried. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Locati on | Require d | Example | If the StartTime Deasncdr i pEtnidoTnime parameters are |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The following examples demonstrate how to determine the period in which monitoring data is queried: If you set the Period parameter to 15, the specified time range must be less than or equal to 20 minutes. For example, if you set the StartTime parameter to 2021- 05-08 08:10:00 and the EndTime parameter to 2021- 05-08 08:30:00, the monitoring data of the last 15 seconds in the time range is queried. If you set the Period parameter to 60 or 900, the specified time range must be less than or equal to 2 hours. For example, if you set the Period parameter to 60, the StartTime parameter to 2021- 05-08 08:00:00, and the EndTime parameter to 2021- 05-08 10:00:00, the monitoring data of the last 60 seconds in the time range is queried. |

Example: 1508136760000. |

Valid values: 0: reports raw data 1: reports aggregate data We recommend that you report aggregate data in both the aggregation periods of 60 s and 300 s. ##### 4.1.4.2 PutResourceMetricRule

Configures a threshold-triggered alert rule for a performance metric of a resource. For more information about example values of the cloud service parameters, such as `Namespace` , `MetricName` , and `Dimensions` , see Appendix 1: Metrics.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | PutResourceMet ricRule | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to PutResourceMetricRule. |
| ContactGroups | String | Yes | Default alert contact group | The alert contact group. Note Separate multiple alert contact groups with commas (,). |
| MetricName | String | Yes | cpu total _ | The metric name. Note For more information, see Appendix 1: Metrics. |
| Namespace | String | Yes | acs ecs dashbo _ _ ard | The namespace of the cloud service. Note For more information, see Appendix 1: Metrics. |
| Resources | String | Yes | [{"instanceId":"x xxxxxx"}] | The resource for which an alert is triggered based on the alert rule. Note For more information, see Dimensions in Appendix 1: Metrics. |

| RuleId | String | Yes | a151cd6023eac ee2f0978e0386 3cc1697c89508 **** | The ID of the alert rule. Note The ID is generated by the caller. You can specify an existing ID to modify the corresponding alert rule or specify a new ID to create an alert rule. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RuleName | String | Yes | My alert rule | The name of the alert rule. |
| Webhook | String | No | http://ww.aliyun. com | The callback URL to which a POST request is sent when an alert is triggered based on the alert rule. |
| EffectiveInterv al | String | No | 00:00-23:59 | The time period during which the alert rule is effective. |
| NoEffectiveInt erval | String | No | 00:00-06:00 | The time period during which the alert rule is ineffective. |
| SilenceTime | Integer | No | 86400 | The mute period during which alerts are not reported even if the trigger conditions are met. Unit: seconds. Default value: 86400, which is equivalent to one day. Note Only one alert notification is sent during each mute period even if the metric value continuously exceeds the threshold of the alert rule. |
| Interval | String | No | 60 | The interval at which the system checks whether the alert rule is triggered. The default value is the lowest frequency at which the metric is polled. Unit: seconds. Note For more information about the frequency at which monitoring data is collected, see DescribeMetricMetaList. |

| EmailSubject | String | No |   | An alert triggered | The subject of the alert notification email. |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Period | String | No |   | 60 | The aggregation cycle of monitoring data. The value is an integer multiple of 60. Unit: seconds. The default value is the frequency at which monitoring data is collected. |   |   |
| Escalations.Cri tical.Statistics | String | No |   | Average | The statistical methods for Critical- level alerts. |   |   |
| Escalations.Cri tical.Comparis onOperator | String | No |   |   | The operator that is used to compare the metric value with the threshold for Critical-level alerts. Valid values: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold : greater than or equal to the threshold GreaterThanThreshold : greater than the threshold LessThanOrEqualToThreshold : less than or equal to the threshold LessThanThreshold : less than the threshold NotEqualToThreshold : not equal to the threshold GreaterThanYesterday : greater than the metric value at the same time yesterday LessThanYesterday : less than the metric value at the same time yesterday GreaterThanLastWeek : greater than the metric value at the same time last week LessThanLastWeek : less than the metric value at the same time last week GreaterThanLastPeriod : greater than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle LessThanLastPeriod : less than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold |   |
|   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrE qualToThreshold |   |   |   |
| Escalations.Cri tical.Threshold | String | No |   | 90 | The threshold for Critical-level alerts. |   |   |

| Escalations.Cri tical.Times | Integer | No |   | 3 | The consecutive number of times for which the metric value meets the alert condition before a Critical-level alert is triggered. |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Escalations.Wa rn.Statistics | String | No |   | Average | The statistical methods for Warn- level alerts. |   |   |
| Escalations.Wa rn.Comparison Operator | String | No |   |   | The operator that is used to compare the metric value with the threshold for Warn-level alerts. Valid values: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold : greater than or equal to the threshold GreaterThanThreshold : greater than the threshold LessThanOrEqualToThreshold : less than or equal to the threshold LessThanThreshold : less than the threshold NotEqualToThreshold : not equal to the threshold GreaterThanYesterday : greater than the metric value at the same time yesterday LessThanYesterday : less than the metric value at the same time yesterday GreaterThanLastWeek : greater than the metric value at the same time last week LessThanLastWeek : less than the metric value at the same time last week GreaterThanLastPeriod : greater than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle LessThanLastPeriod : less than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold |   |
|   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrE qualToThreshold |   |   |   |
| Escalations.Wa rn.Threshold | String | No |   | 90 | The threshold for Warn-level alerts. |   |   |

| Escalations.Wa rn.Times | Integer | No |   | 3 | The consecutive number of times for which the metric value meets the alert condition before a Warn-level alert is triggered. |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Escalations.Inf o.Statistics | String | No |   | Average | The statistical methods for Info-level alerts. |   |   |
| Escalations.Inf o.Comparison Operator | String | No |   |   | The operator that is used to compare the metric value with the threshold for Info-level alerts. Valid values: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold : greater than or equal to the threshold GreaterThanThreshold : greater than the threshold LessThanOrEqualToThreshold : less than or equal to the threshold LessThanThreshold : less than the threshold NotEqualToThreshold : not equal to the threshold GreaterThanYesterday : greater than the metric value at the same time yesterday LessThanYesterday : less than the metric value at the same time yesterday GreaterThanLastWeek : greater than the metric value at the same time last week LessThanLastWeek : less than the metric value at the same time last week GreaterThanLastPeriod : greater than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle LessThanLastPeriod : less than the metric value in the last monitoring cycle |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold |   |
|   |   |   |   | GreaterThanOrE qualToThreshold |   |   |   |
| Escalations.Inf o.Threshold | String | No |   | 90 | The threshold for Info-level alerts. |   |   |

ALARM TEMPLATE FIRS _ _ T: The metrics specified in the alert template take precedence. ### 4.2 Metrics for Apsara Stack services

**services**

The cloud services that are connected to CloudMonitor have different metrics. When you call CloudMonitor API operations to query the metrics of a cloud service, you must specify the metrics that are supported by the namespace of the cloud service, and specify the monitoring dimensions and intervals. The dimensions and intervals supported by each metric of a cloud service vary from each other.

**Usage notes**

You can call CloudMonitor API operations to query metric data of the last 31 days. The value of **Dimensions** is a JSON string in the format of `{"instanceId":"<Instance ID of`

```
an Apsara Stack service>"} .
```

When you call a CloudMonitor API operation, you must set **Namespace** and **Period**.

**Elastic computing**

**Elastic Compute Service (ECS)**

**Basic metrics**

Set **Namespace** to **acs_ecs_dashboard**. Set **Period** to an integral multiple of 60. Default value: **60**. Unit: seconds.

> **Note:** The following metrics are collected from the virtual host layer and are slightly different from the metrics collected inside the operating system.

| (ECS) InternetOutRate | bits/s | InternetOutRate | userId and instanceId | The rate of outbound traffic over the Internet. |

**Operating system metrics**

Set **Namespace** to **acs_ecs_dashboard**. Set **Period** to an integral multiple of 15. Default value: **15**. Unit: seconds.

> **Note:** For ECS instances, you must install the CloudMonitor agent to collect metrics inside the operating system.
> Installation method: In the left-side navigation pane of the CloudMonitor console, click **Host Monitoring** and set Host Type to ECS. In the ECS monitoring list, select the instances that you want to monitor and click **Batch Install** in the lower part of the page.
> Metric data can be displayed in the monitoring chart in 5 to 10 minutes after the CloudMonitor agent is installed.

PI reference

## 5 STS API reference

### 5.1 AssumeRole

Obtains a Security Token Service (STS) token to assume a Resource Access Management (RAM) role.

**Request header**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Loca tion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DurationSe conds | Long | Quer y | No | 3600 | The validity period of the STS token. Unit: seconds. Minimum value: 900. Maximum value: the value of the MaxSessionDuration parameter. Default value: 3600. |
| Policy | Strin g | Quer y | No | {"Statement": [{"Action": ["*"],"Effect": "Allow","Resource": ["*"]}],"Version":"1"} | The policy that specifies the permissions of the returned STS token. This allows you to implement more fine-grained access control. The following descriptions provide the details: If you specify this parameter, the permissions that are granted to the STS token are the intersection of the RAM role permissions and the permissions that are specified in this parameter. If you do not specify this parameter, the STS token has all permissions of the RAM role. The value of the parameter must be 1 to 1,024 characters in length. |

PI reference

| RoleArn | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | acs:ram::123456789012* ***:role/adminrole | The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the RAM role. The trusted entity of the RAM role is an Alibaba Cloud account. For more information, see Create a RAM role for a trusted Alibaba Cloud account or CreateRole. Format: acs:ram:: <account id>:role/<role _ _ name>. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RoleSessio nName | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | alice | The name of the role session. Set this parameter based on your business requirements. In most cases, you can set this parameter to the identity of the API caller. For example, you can specify a username. In ActionTrail logs, you can use the RoleSessionName value to distinguish different users who assume the same RAM role to perform operations. This way, you can perform user-specific auditing. The value must be 2 to 64 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, and the following special characters: .@- . _ |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 6894B13B-6D71- 4EF5-88FA- F32781734A7F | The request ID. |
| Credentials | Struct |   | The access credentials. |

PI reference

| -SecurityToken | String | ******** | The STS token. Note: Alibaba Cloud STS does not impose limits on the length of STS tokens. We recommend that you do not specify a maximum length for an STS token. |
|---|---|---|---|
| - AccessKeySecr et | String | ****************************************** | The AccessKey secret. |
| -AccessKeyId | String | STS.L4aBSCSJVMuK g5U1**** | The AccessKey ID. |
| -Expiration | String | 2015-04- 09T11:52:19Z | The time when the STS token expires. The time is displayed in UTC. |
| AssumedRoleU ser | Struct |   | The temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |
| -Arn | String | acs:ram::12345678 9012****:role/admi nrole/alice | The ARN of the temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |
| - AssumedRoleI d | String | 34458433936495* ***:alice | The ID of the temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
http(s)://[Endpoint]/?Action=AssumeRole &RoleArn=acs:ram::123456789012****:role/adminrole &RoleSessionName=alice &<Common request parameters>
```

Sample success responses `JSON` format PI reference `{`

```json
 "RequestId":"6894B13B-6D71-4EF5-88FA-F32781734A7F",
 "AssumedRoleUser":{
  "Arn":"acs:ram::123456789012****:role/adminrole/alice
```

`",`

```json
  "AssumedRoleId":"34458433936495****:alice"
```

`},`

```json
 "Credentials":{
  "SecurityToken":"********",
  "AccessKeyId":"STS.L4aBSCSJVMuKg5U1****",
  "AccessKeySecret":"****************************************",
  "Expiration":"2015-04-09T11:52:19Z"
```

### 5.2 GetCallerIdentity

Queries the identity of the current requester.

**Request header**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

PI reference

| IdentityType | String | RAMUser | The identity type. Valid values: Account: an Alibaba Cloud account RAMUser: a Resource Access Management (RAM) user AssumedRoleUser: a RAM role |
| AccountId | String | 196813200012**** | The ID of the Alibaba Cloud account to which the current requester belongs. |
| RequestId | String | 3C87BF47-3724- 5443-ADC1- 5AEAD9A03EB1 | The request ID. |
| PrincipalId | String | 28877424437521* *** | The ID of the principal. |
| UserId | String | 216959339000**** | The user ID. The following descriptions provide the details: If the requester uses an Alibaba Cloud account to call the operation, the ID of the Alibaba Cloud account is returned. If the requester uses a RAM user to call the operation, the ID of the RAM user is returned. This parameter is returned only if the current requester uses an Alibaba Cloud account or a RAM user. |
| Arn | String | acs:ram::19681320 0012****:user/adm in | The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the current requester. |
| RoleId | String | 33537620082992* *** | The ID of the RAM role. This parameter is returned only if the current requester uses a RAM role. |
